summary: This bill ends the 287(g) program by amending the Immigration and Nationality Act to restrict all authority to investigate, arrest, or detain people for immigration violations to federal immigration officers and DHS employees only.

scores.thoughts: The bill rescinds 287(g) authority for state/local immigration enforcement but contains no provisions altering federal spending levels, appropriations, or budgets. It is silent on fiscal matters.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No relation to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends the INA to eliminate 287(g) agreements, stripping state and local officers of authority to investigate, arrest, or detain for immigration violations and declaring immigration enforcement an exclusively federal function. This removes a key decentralized enforcement mechanism that has been used to expand interior enforcement and border-adjacent cooperation. By narrowing who may enforce immigration law, the bill reduces enforcement capacity and tools rather than expanding them, moving the policy in the direction of less restriction and more limited enforcement reach.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense spending or policy.
No environmental or regulatory provisions.
No provisions on welfare programs, entitlements, or benefits.
No education-related content.
No drug enforcement or decriminalization measures.
While the bill concerns arrest and detention authority, it is narrowly limited to immigration violations and does not address broader criminal sentencing, policing practices, or justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No fiscal or debt-related language.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ protections or rights.
No foreign aid provisions.
No election or voting provisions.
No technology, data, or privacy provisions.
No labor or union provisions.
No religious liberty or anti-discrimination provisions.
